detail:
MedlinePlus describes adenomyosis as a thickening of the walls of the uterus. It occurs when endometrial tissue, which forms the lining of the uterus, grows into the outer muscular walls of the uterus. The cause is not known, and MedlinePlus notes that adenomyosis may sometimes cause the uterus to grow in size. The condition most often occurs in women ages 35 to 50 who have had at least one pregnancy.

In many cases, there are no symptoms. When symptoms occur, MedlinePlus lists prolonged or heavy menstrual bleeding, painful menstrual periods that get worse, and pelvic pain during intercourse. On a pelvic exam, a provider may find a soft and slightly enlarged uterus. An ultrasound of the uterus may be done, though it may not give a clear diagnosis, and an MRI can help distinguish adenomyosis from other uterine tumors; MedlinePlus notes the only way to confirm the diagnosis is by examining uterine tissue after surgery to remove the uterus.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about adenomyosis symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: MedlinePlus describes adenomyosis as a thickening of the walls of the uterus that occurs when endometrial tissue grows into the outer muscular walls of the uterus, most often in women ages 35 to 50 who have had at least one pregnancy.
takeaways: adenomyosis is endometrial tissue growing into the muscular uterine wall
many cases cause no symptoms; heavy bleeding and worsening period pain can occur
ultrasound may not be conclusive; mri can help tell it apart from other growths
title: Adenomyosis: when uterine lining tissue grows into the uterine wall
